body.en:
Question B-008-001-011.

Why the correct answer is right: A suitable receiver-input filter can reduce the strong unwanted signals before they reach the non-linear receiver stage where mixing occurs. Filtering early is like stopping dirt at the door instead of cleaning it up later.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Common-mode choke": A common-mode choke helps with RF current on cable shields or leads, but it is not the main selective cure for two transmitters mixing inside a VHF receiver.
- sourceIndex 2: "RF attenuator": An RF attenuator may reduce overload, but it reduces the desired VHF signal by the same amount. A selective receiver filter is the better answer when the problem transmitters can be rejected before the mixer.
- sourceIndex 3: "Narrow band IF filter": A narrow intermediate-frequency (IF) filter works after the front-end mixing has already happened, so it cannot stop the intermodulation product from being created.
